mismatch.varies: the CA (the system bundle instead of the Puppet CA), which did not sign the node's certificate

action.mutates: on the peer: installs rsyslog-gnutls, copies its own Puppet CA, certificate and key to /etc/rsyslog.d/p8test-tls (syslog-readable), adds /etc/rsyslog.d/10-p8test-server.conf (an imtcp gtls listener on 6514, x509/certvalid, writing what it receives to /var/log/p8test-remote.log) and restarts rsyslog
restarts rsyslog on the node, logs `p8test-rsyslog-forward-token` with tag p8test-rsyslog through logger, then waits 5 s
none beyond reading the peer's received log (declared mutating so it runs after the node's line was sent)
notes rsyslog's main PID and its journal cursor in /run/p8test-rsyslog/before-rule, then appends a comment line to /etc/rsyslog.d/40-forward.conf on the node
none beyond reading the rule, rsyslog's state and its journal (declared mutating so it runs after the node's agent run)

outcomes.outcome: the forwarding rule sends every facility and severity to the target over TLS with the node's certificate, key and CA, validating the server's certificate
the target is pinned in /etc/hosts when its IP is given
a line logged on the node reaches the remote TLS log server, under the node's name
a changed forwarding rule is restored by the next agent run, which restarts rsyslog once
the failover target (forwarding switches to it while the first target is suspended), forward_auth_log and check_names

uncovered.why: fixture variants: the fixture forwards to one live target and sets none of them; failover needs a second fixture (a dead target, the peer as failover), which one set cannot hold; untested
